ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories. The Cayman Exempted Company’s UBOs must be identified to the Gibraltar registered agent at 25% plus control-based attribution. Screening is conducted against the Gibraltar sanctions list published by GFIU, the UK OFSI Consolidated List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and the Cayman Islands sanctions references. PEP status, adverse media, tax crime indicators, corroborated source of wealth, and source of funds are verified with independent electronic checks, notarized passports, and bank/corporate references. Non-face-to-face e-commerce formation requires enhanced due diligence because the settlement rails include Airwallex, Stripe, and Amazon Pay. Suspicious activity must be reported to GFIU under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 within the statutory reporting window; records are retained for at least five years from business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House – official online name availability and incorporation portal: https://www.companieshouse.gi; paper filings are lodged with the Registrar of Companies, 9/10 Library Ramp, Gibraltar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official commercial and filing language is English. Company and overseas-company names must be expressed in Roman (Latin) alphabet characters, numerals, and permitted symbols. Non-English trading names, including Chinese pinyin transliterations, are accepted only in Roman-alphabet transliteration and must be accompanied by a certified English translation of the constitutional documents where the foreign-language name is embedded in the instrument. The Registrar will reject names that are not readily identifiable, are misleading, or create confusion with an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the Registrar must give written grounds. The applicant has 14 calendar days to file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar together with evidence of any regulatory consent and a corrected name proposal. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file an administrative appeal petition in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar within 42 days of the refusal notice. Where the name contains a sensitive token, written prior approval of the Minister for Financial Services is required, and the Minister’s refusal is subject only to judicial review. Legal representation by a Gibraltar-admitted lawyer is required for any judicial review. During the appeal, the applicant may reserve an alternative name for a new 30-day window to mitigate delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A qualified virtual office is acceptable for this unregulated Amazon FBA trading structure: the Cayman Exempted Company, when registered as an overseas company in Gibraltar, must maintain a registered office and an address for service of process at a physical Gibraltar location supplied by a licensed corporate services provider. A pure electronic mailbox or non-physical virtual address is not accepted. The GFSC AML/CFT framework requires the registered agent’s physical location to be the point of custody for statutory registers, the beneficial ownership register, and AML documentation. This arrangement is permissible for the ISIC 4791 online marketplace seller because no statutory license is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 12-18% annual probability of a routine Registrar or GFIU compliance inspection for a non-regulated e-commerce overseas company in Gibraltar. The probability rises to 55-70% if a suspicious activity report is filed, a PSP account is terminated, or risk flags emerge at the payment-rail onboarding stage (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex). Unannounced physical premise inspections are rare but possible at approximately 5-8% likelihood, and intensify if the registered office is used by multiple unrelated companies or if the UBO screening outcome is adverse.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (as revised, 2021 Revision), Section 14 (Exempted Companies), Section 16 (Registered Office) and Section 18 (Formalities of Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (General Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association, Form 1 (Incorporation Application), and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or escrow capital requirement; the authorised share capital may be set at a nominal amount (commonly USD 1.00). No capital injection or bank escrow is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscriber shares be issued to the initial subscriber in accordance with the Company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, fully paid to the extent of the capital subscribed as set forth in the register of members. 2. The Company’s registered office be adopted at the office of the licensed registered agent, c/o [Registered Office Provider], [Address, Grand Cayman], and the registered agent be authorised to file the registered office notice. 3. The following persons be and are hereby appointed as officers of the Company: [Name], Director; [Name], Secretary; each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until removed by resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cayman Company Name Clearance and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (General Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance application to the Registrar indicating the company will be an exempted company under Section 14 and that it will not trade within the Cayman Islands except as permitted. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and must not be prohibited or misleading. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 90 days. A licensed registered agent files the application and awaits the name clearance certificate.
required_dossiers: Name clearance application (prescribed form)
Copy of subscriber's passport / due diligence
Registered agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, promptly re-submit with an alternate name; no formal appeal period exists, so immediate correction and re-submission is the standard cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Cayman Registered Agent / Corporate Services Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct corporate counsel to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the subscriber declaration, and initial director consent. The sole subscriber executes the M&A before a witness. The registered agent then compiles the incorporation package and submits it to the Registrar for approval.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber information (full legal name, address, date of birth)
Consent to act as first director
Cayman registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries a discrepancy, the registered agent corrects the M&A by re-execution or files written explanations; if the subscriber is deemed unsuitable, a replacement subscriber is engaged before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (Registry Fees and Incorporation Fulfilment Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent pays the prescribed government incorporation and exemption fees via the Registrar's online payment system and attests to the accuracy of the filing. Once the Registrar verifies full compliance, the Certificate of Incorporation under Section 14 is issued. Certified copies are obtained for use in Gibraltar filing and banking.
required_dossiers: Incorporation fee payment receipt
Filed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name clearance certificate
Registered office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is placed in query, the agent pays any fees shortfall or penalty within ten working days, or submits a request for correction to the Registry; unresolved queries may require a fresh incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Statutory Registered Office and Registered Agent in the Cayman Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (Registered Office Administration Unit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registered Office Notice (Form RO1) appointing a licensed corporate services provider located in the Cayman Islands as the registered office. The provider undertakes statutory record-keeping, filing of annual returns, and maintenance of the registered agent obligations under the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Form RO1 (Registered Office Notice)
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Registered agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address or provider is rejected, promptly select a different licensed provider and re-file the Notice; continued non-compliance may lead to involuntary strike-off.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organizational Meeting and Statutory Governance Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors (with Corporate Services Provider as Minute Clerk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, or use a circular written resolution, to adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering allotment of subscriber shares, adoption of registered office, and officer appointments. Confirm issuance of share certificates, creation of statutory registers, and authorisation for future banking relationships in Gibraltar or UK EMI.
required_dossiers: Notice of first meeting or written resolution consent
First board resolution text
Consent to act for each appointed officer/director
Register of members, directors, and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment or resolution is invalidly carried, an emergency board resolution may be passed to ratify or reverse the decision; any irregularity in share issue is cured by a supplemental board minute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Cayman Exempted Company as an External Company in Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of establishing a place of business or commencing regulated activities in Gibraltar, file Form EO (External Company Registration) with the Gibraltar Registrar. Include certified and apostilled copies of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation and M&A, a list of directors/secretary, the Gibraltar registered office address, and appointment of an authorised local agent for service of process. Pay the external company registration fee to obtain a Gibraltar registered number.
required_dossiers: Form EO (Registration of External Company)
Certified copy of Cayman Certificate of Incorporation (apostilled)
Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles (apostilled)
List of directors and secretary (with current particulars)
Consent to act of Gibraltar agent for service of process
Proof of Gibraltar registered office address
Government filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects to the name or documentation, the applicant may file a correction set with additional legalisation or adopt a distinct Gibraltar trade name; the statutory one-month deadline is temporarily suspended during official query resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing activity is carried out; ISIC 4791 covers online marketplace retail without physical goods processing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license required — this is a non-physical online marketplace (Amazon FBA) business and the target metadata confirms no statutory license requirement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Agency (Gibraltar) / Department of the Environment — not applicable to this digital retail activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical project, site development, or environmental intervention exists; no EIA screening or registration triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for remote e-commerce; if Amazon FBA fulfillment centers are used, the facility operator (Amazon) remains responsible for all wastewater, VOC, and waste handling compliance under local UK/EU law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No physical workplace in Cayman or Gibraltar requiring fire safety certification or structural load inspection. The Gibraltar registered office, if staffed, must comply with the Gibraltar Building (Fire Safety) Regulations and the Occupational Safety and Health Act; no goods-handling or industrial permits are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax — Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar; customs: HM Customs Gibraltar. Official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/en/taxation
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman Exempted Company without physical presence or local-source activity in Gibraltar is not automatically required to hold a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN). If the entity establishes a place of business (including warehousing, staff, or permanent commercial presence for Amazon FBA operations), it must: (1) register the overseas company with the Gibraltar Companies Registry under the Companies (Overseas Companies) Ordinance; (2) apply to the Commissioner of Income Tax for a TRN after company registration; (3) obtain a customs registration with HM Customs Gibraltar for any import/export declarations. Because Gibraltar has no VAT/GST, no VAT identification number is issued; the TRN is the sole statutory tax identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or entity-classification election exists in Gibraltar. Tax residence is fact-based: a company managed and controlled in Gibraltar is resident and taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident company (including a Cayman Exempted Company managed outside Gibraltar) is taxed only on Gibraltar-source income. No hybrid mismatch elections are available; OECD BEPS/ATAD-aligned anti-hybrid rules apply automatically. A foreign company can rely on the territorial limitation without filing any formal election but must disclose non-resident status in its tax return if registered.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / No GST / No Sales and Use Tax (Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT territory; only import and excise duties apply under the Customs & Excise regime)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST regime and therefore no turnover threshold. Importers/declarants must be registered with HM Customs Gibraltar for import/export declarations; no minimum economic threshold applies. Excise licences are required for alcohol, tobacco and hydrocarbon oils.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, e-invoicing API, or digital stamping requirement. Customs entries are submitted electronically to HM Customs Gibraltar and supporting commercial invoices/packing lists must be retained for audit; Amazon FBA marketplace documentation follows Amazon's seller portal, not a Gibraltar fiscal invoice regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — Gibraltar does not levy VAT/GST, so no VAT zero-rating or VAT refund mechanism exists for goods or services. Exports from Gibraltar are generally not subject to Gibraltar export duty; export customs declarations apply only to controlled, excise, or strategically regulated goods. The Cayman entity's foreign-source e-commerce sales are outside Gibraltar's tax net.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (HM Customs Gibraltar electronic single-entry document)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / carrier tracking evidence
Amazon FBA shipment manifest and customs brokerage records
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice evidencing cross-border funds receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback exists. Under the Gibraltar Customs Ordinance, false declarations, misdescription, or fraudulent export entries attract forfeiture of goods and/or penalties of up to three times the value of the goods, plus criminal liability (imprisonment) for fraudulent evasion. Duty reliefs and exemptions are subject to retrospective audit by HM Customs Gibraltar with recovery of unpaid duty and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the integrated financial regulator, acting alongside the Bank of England monetary framework; Gibraltar Pound (GIP) is issued by the Government of Gibraltar under the Currency Notes Act 1934 and is pegged at 1:1 to GBP Sterling. No separate Gibraltar central bank exists; exchange-rate and monetary policy de facto follow HMT/BoE parameters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. Gibraltar maintains no exchange-control legislation; GIP and GBP circulate interchangeably. For a Cayman Exempted Company there is likewise no Cayman Islands capital-control restriction; profits, dividends and liquidation proceeds may be remitted freely to Gibraltar or any other banking corridor. Remittance hurdles are limited to standard AML/CFT documentation, UK tax transparency forms (CRS/FATCA) and confirmation of economic substance status in the Cayman Islands. No Gibraltar withholding tax applies to dividends, interest, royalties or management fees, and no exchange-rate authorization or central-bank clearance is required for any transfer size.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Gibraltar and the United Kingdom impose no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime; no mandatory conversion ratio applies and no deadline exists for repatriation of export receipts. Amazon FBA sales proceeds may be retained offshore in foreign currency, converted freely, or pooled in GBP/GIP accounts at the taxpayer's election.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Private Banking / Wealth Management Liquidity Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Restricted-Medium. Gibraltar-regulated FinTech and EMI institutions are scarce for marketplace sellers; most viable rails are UK FCA-authorised EMIs (Airwallex, Stripe, Payoneer, WorldFirst) accessed by the Cayman entity through a Gibraltar operational address. Legal acceptance is conditional on the EMI's own cross-border acceptance policy: UK FCA EMIs may on-board Cayman Exempted Companies only under enhanced due diligence, requiring proof of Cayman economic substance, source-of-funds dossiers and a demonstrable Gibraltar nexus. Cayman-incorporated Amazon FBA sellers are frequently declined by automated onboarding engines; a Gibraltar-branch virtual account or an interposed Gibraltar management company materially raises approval rates. Airwallex and Stripe remain the preferred clearing aggregators for marketplace receivables, but principal cross-border treasury banking should be held at a Gibraltar licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar licensed banks uniformly require a physical KYC interview for at least one director or a corporate officer of a Cayman Exempted Company; remote opening is possible only when the UBO holds an existing regulated relationship, all documents are apostilled, and a Gibraltar-licensed corporate service provider co-signs the account mandate. Trusted Novus Bank and GIB may accept a video-conference interview if the applicant's Cayman registered agent and Gibraltar CSP attend remotely with digital ID verification, but a board-level physical presence at the Gibraltar branch remains the compliance default for capital-escrow accounts. Pure digital EMIs (Airwallex/Stripe) permit 100% remote onboarding but impose lower transaction caps and may later freeze flows pending substance re-verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-haven structuring: a Cayman tax-exempt entity seeking a Gibraltar banking passport with ultimate beneficial owners outside the UK/EEA
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cayman Islands Economic Substance Declaration and confirmation of compliance with the International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Act; Cayman beneficial ownership register (BOOM/General Registry) extract; audited financial statements or CIMA-approved exempted-company return; full corporate chart and issued share register; notarised constitutive documents (M&A and Articles); board resolution approving the Gibraltar bank relationship; written commercial rationale evidencing genuine Amazon FBA trade route through Gibraltar as an EU-adjacent logistics and treasury node; and six-months of bank statements from the Cayman funding account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity marketplace receipts through Amazon Pay/Stripe/Airwallex lacking an invoice and VAT trail in the banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amazon Seller Central account certification and marketplace registration documents; UK VAT registration certificate (HMRC) and filed VAT returns covering FBA UK/EU inventory; 24-month platform settlement statements; Airwallex/Stripe transaction histories; a reconciliation mapping each payment rail to specific Amazon orders and FBA warehouse stock movement reports; customs/import declarations (EORI) for goods stored in UK fulfilment centres; and an annual accountant's letter confirming the entity's status as an Amazon FBA general merchandise reseller (ISIC 4791).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-contractual third-party payments and supplier disbursements to high-risk trade counterparties from the Gibraltar operating account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements with each supplier and logistics provider; KYC file on every counterparty including registration documents, physical address and bank account ownership; bills of lading, airway bills, and CMR waybills matching invoice values; commercial invoices and packing lists; documentary evidence of the underlying trade (including purchase orders and marketplace listing URLs); anti-money-laundering source-of-funds declaration for each significant outgoing transfer; and board-approved treasury payment policy limiting third-party disbursements to contracted Amazon FBA supply-chain vendors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocol: (1) Cayman Exempted Company receives equity capital from UBOs via SWIFT MT103 to its Cayman or Gibraltar-facilitated receiving account, using Field 70 narrative 'Share capital contribution – Exempted Company – LEI 549300KY_EX'; (2) no Gibraltar exchange-control approval is required, but the remitting bank must annotate the payment purpose code consistent with Gibraltar banking classification 'Inward Direct Investment – Equity Capital' and the Cayman filing reference if applicable; (3) the Gibraltar operating bank performs a source-of-funds verification packet including board resolution authorising the capital call, share certificates, UBO bank statements, and a certified copy of the Cayman register of members; (4) funds may be held in GIP/GBP/EUR/USD multi-currency accounts without any forced conversion; (5) CRS/FATCA forms (Gibraltar financial account notification and Cayman Common Reporting Standard) must be filed with the respective registries to preserve the entity's tax-transparent status; and (6) initial capital exceeding marketplace working-capital requirements should be parked in a GIB capital-escrow sub-account to clearly separate invested equity from operational Amazon proceeds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) Amazon marketplace fees, FBA logistics charges and customer-refund obligations are discharged through Amazon Pay settlement sweep or via Airwallex GBP/EUR receiving accounts automatically reconciled to seller central; (2) supplier and inventory payments are executed via SWIFT MT103 across the Gibraltar banking network, preferentially through Airwallex's global treasury corridor for mid-market FX conversion and low-cost ~0.3% transaction fees; (3) large or repeat cross-border orders are settled through commercial documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by GIB or Trusted Novus, with sight drafts and full export documentation (invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, insurance certificate) to mitigate counterparty risk in high-risk sourcing corridors; (4) sweeps from EMIs to the Gibraltar operational account are batched daily with full remittance-information fields to preserve an auditable trail; and (5) Amazon does not directly credit a Gibraltar bank account for marketplace proceeds, therefore a UK sort-code receiving account via Airwallex/Stripe is mandatory, with next-day automated sweep into the Gibraltar treasury account to avoid trapped liquidity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward Contracts (GBP/GIP vs USD and EUR) for hedging Amazon receivables against supplier liabilities

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted or exotic currencies where physical settlement is unavailable, executed through the Gibraltar bank's international dealing desk for emerging-market procurement exposure
Cross-Currency Swaps (USD-GBP/EUR-GBP floating-for-floating) to convert long-term FBA inventory financing or shareholder loans into the entity's functional treasury currency
FX Options / Zero-Cost Collars to cap conversion costs on high-volume quarterly Amazon settlement sweeps while preserving upside on GBP appreciation
Same-day and Tomorrow-Next (T/N) FX Swaps with the Gibraltar licensed bank or Airwallex treasury for working-capital optimisation between GIP, GBP, USD and EUR pooled accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Islands Annual Return and Annual Government Fee (standard capital tier: authorized share capital not exceeding KYD 50,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation under the Companies (Amendment) Act 2023; no Registrar reminder is issued.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late charge of KYD 200 (USD 240) if paid within two months, increasing to KYD 300 (USD 360) thereafter; continued default triggers loss of good standing, strike-off from the Register and vesting of the company's assets in the Cayman Islands Government.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Information Authority (TIA), Ministry of Finance, Cayman Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the relevant financial period (on or before 30 June following a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to KYD 10,000 (USD 12,000) for late or inaccurate filing; intentional evasion or false declarations carry imprisonment up to 5 years; data is exchanged with EU and UK tax authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Islands Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS) register update and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS), Cayman Islands General Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial particulars within 14 days of incorporation or of a Registrar notice; updates within 14 days of any shareholding transfer; register accuracy is confirmed with each Annual Return filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to KYD 25,000 (USD 30,000) per contravention plus imprisonment up to 2 years; repeated defaults are referred to the AML supervisor and may lead to involuntary strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return (Confirmation Statement) — overseas company registration under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the end of each 12-month review period measured from the date of Gibraltar registration or the anniversary of the last confirmation statement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties of GIP 50 (USD 68) per month of default up to GIP 300 (USD 410); six months of continuous default leads to compulsory strike-off of the Gibraltar registration and cessation of the foreign company's right to carry on business in Gibraltar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (full return or nil declaration for non-Gibraltar-source Amazon FBA profits)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 September following the end of the Gibraltar tax year (1 July – 30 June), or within 30 days of the Commissioner's assessment notice, whichever applies; a nil return remains mandatory where no Gibraltar-source taxable profit is claimed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts penalties up to 100% of tax assessed plus daily default fines of GIP 100 (USD 136); late payment interest is applied at the statutory rate; persistent non-filing supports assessment by best judgment, director disqualification and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Cayman Islands: a non-regulated exempted company is not subject to statutory audit; audit is triggered only for regulated activities (fund, bank, insurance, trust) or where members holding at least 10% of voting rights require an audit under the Companies Act. Gibraltar: statutory audit is compulsory where the company meets two of three thresholds — turnover exceeding GIP 10.2 million, balance-sheet assets exceeding GIP 5.1 million, or average employees exceeding 50; below these limits, unaudited accounts with a directors' report may be filed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (IASB) is the governing framework in both jurisdictions; the Cayman Companies Act permits IFRS or US GAAP with no public filing of accounts, and the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 requires EU-adopted IFRS for large/listed entities and permits small-company accounting principles below the audit thresholds. Accounting records are maintained on an accrual basis in USD with month-end management pack preparation for the Amazon FBA marketplace, and retained for no fewer than 7 years to cover UK, Gibraltar and Cayman enquiry windows.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Cayman: beneficial ownership particulars are registered in the company's beneficial ownership register held at the registered office and filed through BOSS within 14 days of any shareholding transfer; the corporate service provider verifies the register annually at the time of the Annual Return filing. Gibraltar: as an overseas company, beneficial ownership and block application details are maintained with the Gibraltar Register of Companies; any transfer producing or extinguishing 25%-plus ownership is reported within the annual confirmation cycle, and the non-resident status claimed in the annual tax return is cross-referenced to the same ownership data.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 1,800 per annum for combined Cayman registered office and Gibraltar corporate secretarial agent; USD 350 – USD 900 per annum for a Gibraltar-only compliance agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 9,000 for a full IFRS statutory audit of the single-entity FBA structure; USD 2,000 – USD 4,000 for an unaudited accountant's review engagement under the Cayman audit-exemption and Gibraltar small-company regime.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat on chargeable income (post-2020 unitary rate; small-bands abolished)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax system: foreign-source dividends and interest are exempt; no capital gains tax; no VAT/GST; no municipal or provincial income taxes; statutory capital allowances available under the Income Tax Act 2010. No free-zone tax holidays applicable.
